original_question: Let k be a fixed positive integer and let G be a sufficiently large graph with m edges and no isolated vertices. If lambda(G) >= (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, must G contain a cycle of every length t <= 2k + 2 unless G is isomorphic to S_{m/k + (k+1)/2, k}?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Conjecture 7 of arXiv:2305.10290; this survey entry is the Zhai-Lin-Shu cycle conjecture, and its exact source-paper formulation is Conjecture 1.1, equivalently Conjecture 1.2, in the later cycle paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right mathematical target: k is fixed, G has m edges and no isolated vertices, the threshold is (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, the conclusion asks for cycles of all lengths up to 2k + 2, and the exceptional family is the complete split graph family written in your S_{n,k} notation. Those are exactly the load-bearing parts of the conjecture recorded in the survey and restated in the source-paper equivalents. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
missing_details: The paper means that the size m is sufficiently large, not that the order of G is large; formally, for each fixed k there should exist a threshold M(k) such that the statement is asserted for all m >= M(k). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))

lambda(G) should be defined explicitly as the adjacency spectral radius, i.e. the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of G. The survey uses this adjacency-matrix convention throughout. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
The ambient graph class should be stated: the survey works with simple, undirected, unweighted graphs. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
The variable t should be quantified as an integer cycle length, so the stand-alone version should say 'for every integer t with 3 <= t <= 2k + 2'. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))

The exceptional graph should be defined, not just named: it is the complete split graph K_k ∨ I_{(m - k(k-1)/2)/k}; equivalently, in the survey's split-graph notation, it is S_{m/k + (k+1)/2, k}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))

If one keeps the notation S_{m/k + (k+1)/2, k}, one should note the integrality condition for the exception/equality case: (m - k(k-1)/2)/k must be an integer, equivalently m/k + (k+1)/2 must be an integer. Later literature explicitly remarks that this extremal graph is well-defined only under that divisibility condition. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0196885825001629?utm_source=openai))
The survey records this as a conjecture/open problem, not as a proved theorem. A stand-alone research question should preserve that status. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))

If you want the forbidden-subgraph version, it should be presented only as the paper's explicit equivalent reformulation: maximizing rho(G) over C_{2k+1}-free or C_{2k+2}-free graphs with m edges and no isolated vertices. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195669824000519))
refined_question: For a fixed positive integer k, does there exist M(k) such that whenever m >= M(k) and G is a simple graph with m edges and no isolated vertices whose adjacency spectral radius rho(G) satisfies rho(G) >= (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, the graph G contains a cycle C_t for every integer t with 3 <= t <= 2k + 2, unless G is the complete split graph K_k ∨ I_{(m - k(k-1)/2)/k} (equivalently, S_{m/k + (k+1)/2, k})? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation (explicitly stated as equivalent in the cycle paper): for a fixed positive integer k and all sufficiently large m, every graph G in G(m, C_{2k+1}) ∪ G(m, C_{2k+2})—where G(m, F) denotes the F-free graphs with m edges and no isolated vertices—satisfies rho(G) <= (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, with equality if and only if G ≅ K_k ∨ I_{(m - k(k-1)/2)/k}. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195669824000519))
justification: The draft is aiming at the survey's Section 5 entry on tight spectral conditions for cycles, specifically Conjecture 7. Because the survey itself compresses notation, I cross-checked the original cycle formulation in the dedicated paper where the same statement appears as Conjecture 1.1, is explicitly said to have an equivalent extremal reformulation as Conjecture 1.2, and is then linked to the stronger chord-cycle result Theorem 1.3 and its consequence Theorem 1.4. That nearby context is exactly what fixes the intended meaning of the threshold, the exceptional graph, the role of 'sufficiently large m', and the equivalent forbidden-subgraph formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
